subject.title: iOS: keychain save fails on fresh install (cal save failed / disconnected because it could not securely save)

question: Should the iOS repair preserve the current Keychain-only fail-closed boundary while adding diagnostics and in-app recovery, or adopt another secure credential-storage strategy?
rationale: The root native failure is not yet known, and choosing a fallback or different accessibility/access-group policy changes how a gateway bearer token is protected on user devices.

options.title: Diagnose and retain Keychain
options.body: Capture the redacted OSStatus and entitlements, fix the specific Keychain operation, and add an in-app retry without weakening token protection.

options.title: Approve alternate secure storage
options.body: Define and security-review a different platform-backed credential-storage contract before changing the persistence implementation.

recommendation.title: Diagnose and retain Keychain
recommendation.body: Capture the redacted OSStatus and entitlements, fix the specific Keychain operation, and add an in-app retry without weakening token protection.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue was explicitly routed to @ngutman and available context points to recent adjacent iOS gateway work, although ownership history remains incomplete.
